reason: Realtime callback prohibitions remain hard constraints; implementation must replace the obsolete chunk queue/ring contract with the proven PCM-window contract.
Source, decoder, memory, slot, and seek failures require typed current-generation handling while stale generation/epoch/serial results are ignored.
Window diagnostics are counter/histogram based and source errors are logged off-RT; callback and per-slot logging remain forbidden.
The redesign crosses player ownership, producer lifecycle, callback rendering, settings migration, diagnostics, remote source contracts, and process memory accounting.

Reuse the landed seek serial, playback clock direction, decoder seek capability, RT retire mechanism for whole resources, and existing benchmark infrastructure without preserving the inefficient PCM transport.
The landed serial protocol is the ordering baseline for requested versus callback-applied window seeks.
Non-PCM and whole-window destruction remains off-RT while per-chunk PCM retirement is removed.
PlaybackClock and cache-line-isolated StreamingRtView must be designed once with no duplicate position authority.
OpenedSource capabilities, identity, recovery, policy, probe reuse, and persistent decoder/source behavior must satisfy the remote consumer task.
The existing decode_memory_budget integration and current/pending ownership checks must migrate into one live reservation ledger rather than a second budget.
The landed callback seek ordering, scratch lifecycle, DSP reset, and render paths are the integration and performance baseline.
Current per-block allocation/copy, producer polling, decoder reopen, and full-buffer duplication are the exact behaviors v2 replaces.
StreamingDecoder already owns a seekable format reader and exposes realized current_frame; core extensions must preserve that persistent ownership.
